identity: A Jordanian primary-school civics and national-education multiple-choice bank: 20 items, one per printed line, on Wadi Rum and the Dead Sea, family functions, dialogue skills, road safety, public utilities, social solidarity, and the date King Abdullah II assumed his constitutional powers. Four options per item except one.
law: MCQ BANK (section I): I2 stem ends where the siblings begin, I3 every option is its own unit, I5 internal wa never cuts, 0h never cut inside a stem. 369 real tokens / 99 units = 3.7 per unit.
reasoning: The option count is four on nineteen lines, which is the constant that validates every stem boundary, and the ONE exception is genuine: @259-@284 has only THREE options (using water-saving devices / using an electric heater instead of a solar one / tearing up storybooks after reading them), because the 20 tokens after the 6-token stem divide 6+10+4 and no reading of them yields a fourth. I record that rather than forcing the constant, since 1z says the count is a per-document regularity, not a law. Dangling stems: @78 min (al-khawf wa-l-khajal ... MIN | ahdaf al-hiwar | maharat al-hiwar | khasais al-hiwar | muiqat al-hiwar - four parallel idafa heads), @116 hiya, @194 min irshadat, @297 fi tarikh, and @330 the bare definite article AL left stranded by the printing (hadha mafhum AL | al-marafiq al-amma | ...). @317 also shows a stem beginning with a bare hiya because the question word was lost in the scan - I left it inside the stem rather than treating it as an option. Two lines pair a scenario with judgement options and the stem runs to the end of the question (yalab Usama ... ma huwa tasarruf Usama @134; ayy min al-tali yutabar suluk sahih @150), and there 0h mattered: the stems own internal question does not cut, and the options are full first-person sentences (aqif ala hafat al-shurfa fi al-manzil) which stay whole however long. Date options keep their full span including the era marker m (30 kanun al-thani 1962 m), the same treatment as 5 salawat and 10 nyutn th al-a in the earlier banks.
